# 2010B Question 16 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} the clinical laboratory assessment of liver function.
:::

Also asked in: [2007B Question 15](/content/exams/anzca/2007/B/15/index.qmd#examiner-comments), [2017A Question 15](/content/exams/anzca/2017/A/15/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} laboratory tests by the function or injury they reflect. Explain the physiological basis and relevant time course of each, distinguishing synthetic failure, hepatocellular injury, cholestasis and metabolic consequences.

::: {.structure-headings}
### Synthetic Function: Albumin and Coagulation

### Bilirubin Handling

### Hepatocellular Injury

### Cholestasis

### Metabolic and Other Laboratory Consequences
:::

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**29%** passed this question.

Basic points to include to achieve a pass included a description of the battery of tests commonly referred to as liver function tests; a description of what they tested and an appropriate interpretation of an change.

Extra marks were available for suggestions of more sensitive clinical tests of liver function, (Prothrombin time or INR) and integrating the understanding of common derangements of hepatic function.

Common mistakes included listing all the functions of the liver and discussing how these might be assessed.
:::
